clue.text: One trying to lap American driver

indicators.note: to lap is to wrap or fold round something, so one piece encloses the other

parts.note: someone who tries a thing out is a tester

explanation.surface: A racer is attempting to get a full circuit ahead of a motorist from the States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to lap' is a container signal here, in its sense of enfolding, not the racing sense. 'American' gives letters but also colours the definition: the word is chiefly a US term for a lorry driver.
explanation.definitionFit: Originally the handler of a team of horses, now the US word for a trucker.

clue.text: Some will absorb work such as graphic novel?

indicators.note: to absorb is to take something inside, so the first piece swallows the second

parts.note: some of a thing is a part of it
op is short for opus, a musical or literary work

explanation.surface: A certain number of readers find themselves engrossed by things like comic-book fiction.
explanation.definitionFit: An example by association: the movement of Lichtenstein and Warhol borrowed the bold imagery of comic strips, hence the question mark.

clue.text: Swimmer, one not bad doing backstroke

indicators.note: backstroke is swimming on one's back, whimsically telling us the letters travel backwards

parts.note: the Roman numeral for one is I
something not bad is OK

explanation.surface: Someone in the pool is fairly decent at swimming on their back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'doing backstroke' turns the whole run I + OK round. 'Swimmer' is the crossword way of pointing at a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An ornamental carp, so literally a creature that swims.

clue.text: Maybe Oxford or Cambridge stopped stocking books, not as planned

parts.note: Oxford and Cambridge are examples of a university, uni for short
NT is the New Testament, a set of books of the Bible
something that stopped has ended

explanation.surface: A bookshop in one of the two old university towns no longer carries certain titles, which was not the idea.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: something accidental was not meant to happen.

clue.text: Agreement wrongdoer should get tagged when picked up

parts.note: con is slang for a convict

indicators.note: to pick something up is to hear it, so the word is taken by ear

parts.note: an offender who is electronically tagged is tracked

explanation.surface: It is settled that the offender will be fitted with an electronic tag once arrested.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when picked up' asks for a word heard, not arrested: TRACKED is heard as TRACT. In Britain a 'tag' is the ankle monitor fitted to offenders.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a legally binding deal between parties.

clue.text: Scrap unfashionable dish

parts.note: a rag is a scrap of cloth
what is out is no longer in fashion

explanation.surface: Take a dated recipe off the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a richly seasoned stew of meat and vegetables.

clue.text: Escape from Coventry

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the city's name, where they sit in a row

explanation.surface: Someone gets away from a city in the English Midlands.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb or noun: gas or anger gets out through an outlet.

clue.text: Draws attention to offences involving drug

indicators.note: involving means including, so the first piece has the second within it

parts.note: slights are insults, small offences against someone
pot is slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A report highlights crimes connected with narcotics.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: to pick something out with a strong beam so everyone notices it.

clue.text: Anyway, don't stare so much

definitions.meaning: an instruction, read as two words, to look at something to a smaller degree

explanation.definitionFit: One word for 'in any case' that also splits whimsically into a command to gaze not as often.

clue.text: Spending money: cent remains

parts.note: ash is what remains after a fire

explanation.surface: After paying out, a single small coin is all that is left.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remains' reads as a verb in the surface but is the noun for what a fire leaves.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: notes and coins, ready funds for buying things.

clue.text: Order to emulate Ben Hur star? That's not on

parts.note: to emulate someone is, loosely, to be them

indicators.note: that's not tells us the letters named next are absent from the actor's name

parts.note: Charlton Heston played the title role in the 1959 film Ben-Hur
taken as written

explanation.surface: A director tells an actor to copy the lead of a famous epic film, which is simply not acceptable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That's not on' sounds like a complaint about bad behaviour, but 'That's not' is a removal signal and 'on' the two letters the actor's surname loses.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a command, as in doing something at someone's bidding.

clue.text: Property for leasing in Philadelphia belonging to mom?

parts.note: Philadelphia is in Pennsylvania, whose postal abbreviation is PA
a rental is a property let out to tenants

explanation.surface: A flat to let in an American city is owned by somebody's mother.
explanation.walkthrough: The wordplay is whimsical: a let property in Philadelphia would be a 'PA rental'. The American spelling 'mom' matches the American setting.
explanation.definitionFit: An example, hence the question mark: something of a mother's or a father's.

clue.text: The monster slain far down below

indicators.note: something slain is destroyed, so these letters are broken up and rebuilt

explanation.surface: A hero has killed the beast in the deep underworld.
explanation.definitionFit: A superlative synonym: lowest of all, at the very bottom.

clue.text: Sin initially expiated by bishop

indicators.note: initially points at the opening letter of the word beside it

parts.note: RR is Right Reverend, the title of a bishop

explanation.surface: A churchman starts by atoning for a wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: to go astray or do wrong.

clue.text: Name your initial drink

parts.note: a brand is a trade name

indicators.note: initial points at the opening letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: A host asks a guest to say what they would like first from the bar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Name' reads as an imperative verb but is a noun, and 'initial' picks the first letter of 'your'.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a spirit distilled from wine.

clue.text: Heading off, bald eagle approaching unknown island

indicators.note: with its heading off, the next word loses its opening letter

parts.note: taken as written before losing its front
an erne is a sea eagle
y is a letter used for an unknown quantity in algebra

explanation.surface: A great American bird of prey sets out and nears uncharted land in the sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heading off' beheads only 'bald'. A solver wants the bald eagle as one bird; the two words split, and 'eagle' alone gives the sea bird.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the northernmost of the inhabited Channel Islands, between England and France.

clue.text: Hide clubs during coup

indicators.note: during means in the middle of, so the second piece falls within the first

parts.note: a coup is a seizure of power, a takeover
C is the abbreviation for the card suit clubs

explanation.surface: Rebels stash their weapons away while seizing power.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb phrase: to shelter out of sight from danger.

clue.text: A wine brought round grand northern French city

indicators.note: brought round means placed about, so the wine word goes about the next piece

parts.note: vino is an informal word for wine
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A bottle is delivered to a splendid town in the north of France.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the Provencal town famed for its bridge and its popes.

clue.text: Second dish of spicy food will make you run

parts.note: a curry is a spiced dish of Indian origin

explanation.surface: Another helping of something hot sends a diner dashing off.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as a verb: to move with short hurried steps.

clue.text: Cleric's record is carved principally onto stone

indicators.note: in a down entry, pieces placed onto another sit above it

parts.note: an EP is an extended-play record

indicators.note: principally points at the leading letter of the word before it

parts.note: an opal is a precious stone

explanation.surface: A churchman's achievements are mostly chiselled into a slab.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjectival sense: of or relating to a bishop, a senior member of the clergy.

clue.text: Like the lining of one lung or two, might one say?

definitions.text: Like the lining of one lung

indicators.note: might one say tells us the word is spoken, and matched by ear

parts.note: a count of two, more than one, is plural in grammar

explanation.surface: Someone muses on the membrane of a single lung, or of the pair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'might one say' marks a word matched by ear: 'two' as opposed to 'one' is PLURAL, heard as the entry. The surface ties both halves to the lungs.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective for the pleura, the membrane that wraps each lung.

clue.text: Leaders in education keen to appear in photo of teacher

indicators.note: to appear in something is to be seen inside it, so these pieces go within the photo word

parts.note: pic is short for picture
the leading two letters of the word education are E and D
agog means eager and excited

explanation.surface: Head teachers are eager to be seen in a snapshot of one of the staff.
explanation.definitionFit: Adjectival sense: relating to the art and practice of instructing pupils.

clue.text: Sappers are not convinced it provides temporary defence

parts.note: the Sappers are the Royal Engineers of the British Army, abbreviated RE
people who are not convinced doubt

explanation.surface: Army engineers are sceptical that a structure will hold the enemy off for long.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: a small, often hastily built fortification.

clue.text: Rail transport conveying green rock

indicators.note: a vehicle conveying something carries it inside, so the first piece carries the second

parts.note: a train is transport that runs on rails
vert is the heraldic word for green

explanation.surface: A goods wagon carries a load of emerald-coloured stone.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: a pale limestone deposited by mineral springs, used in building.

clue.text: Current supplier developed local site

indicators.note: a developed site has been built over and changed, so these letters are rebuilt

explanation.surface: The present energy company has built on a nearby plot of land.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Current' reads as present-day but means electrical.
explanation.definitionFit: A descriptive definition: a transformer producing high-voltage alternating electricity.

clue.text: Academic thus tours chief city of California on railway

indicators.note: in a down entry, what stands on other pieces sits above them
to tour is to go round, so the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: so means thus
Los Angeles, known as LA

explanation.surface: A professor accordingly visits the main town of a US state by train.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym as an adjective: learned, devoted to serious study.

clue.text: English king welcoming not a single queen

indicators.note: to welcome someone is to take them in, so the king's name takes in the next piece

parts.note: Lear is Shakespeare's tragic king
not a single one means no, as in no entries

explanation.surface: A monarch of England is receiving no royal consort at all.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the name of several royal consorts, such as the one of Aquitaine married to Henry II.

clue.text: Indecisive, swapping one article for another in journal

indicators.text: swapping one article for another in
indicators.note: one grammatical article in the journal word is replaced by a different one

parts.note: a diary is a daily journal
the indefinite article taken out
the definite article put in its place

explanation.surface: An editor cannot make up their mind, exchanging one piece for a different one in the magazine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'swapping one article for another in' replaces the A of DIARY with THE; 'article' is the grammatical kind, not a magazine piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A synonym: wavering, unable to settle on a choice.

clue.text: Hunter's exploit over a long period

indicators.note: in a down entry, the piece over the others sits above them

parts.note: an exploit is a notable act or deed
an eon is an immensely long stretch of time

explanation.surface: A huntsman's daring feat stretches across many years.
explanation.definitionFit: An example from Greek myth: the huntsman turned into a stag by Artemis and killed by his own hounds.

clue.text: Dog to fasten up and put on lead

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word before it is read from the bottom

parts.note: to sew is to fasten with stitches
to put an animal on a lead is to tie it, to tether it

explanation.surface: An owner is told to secure the pet and clip on its leash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns SEW into WES in a down entry. 'Lead' is the British word for a leash.
explanation.definitionFit: An example: the familiar name for a West Highland white terrier.
